supersedesRowStatusOnly.whyItCannotStand: R-4/the program's own code-done-vs-customer-done rule: a close that says 'closed' must be PASS for every parcel of its row on a cited surface-probe artifact. The lane's close DEFERRED the P-175 probe to the planner ('surfaceProbeRowsP175': 'DEFERRED to the planner's own run'). The planner ran it: FAIL 0/5. The lane's own pre-registered falsifier -- 'If node scripts/surface-probe.mjs --rows P-175 reads anything but PASS on all five, name the leg' -- therefore FIRED. Only the row-status field is superseded here; the lane's body of work, PRs, run ids and cell diffs are accepted (see verifiedTrue).

secondFailingLeg_labelOnVacantLots.detail: For 48209:97651/97652/97653/97657 the panel's situs is empty and the P-175 label regex `^(615|617|619|627)\s+STURGEON` cannot match. These lots are vacant with no house number on the CAD roll (the probe's own ADDRESSES metadata says so, and the corrected record situs for them is the house-number-less 'STURGEON DR, SAN MARCOS, TX 78666'). So even a fully crosswalked situs cannot satisfy the label leg for these four. This is an instrument-vs-data tension the overseer should rule on (widen the label leg for vacant lots, or accept that only house-numbered lots can PASS the label leg) -- it is named, not silently worked around.
secondFailingLeg_labelOnVacantLots.note: 629 (the house-numbered lot) DOES now carry the correct label and IS one of the lot's identifiers, and its county polygon at the address point IS the lot. So on identity/label grounds 629 is correct; only the recordPoint leg blocks it.
